research.proposedTitle: Meta's $50 billion plan and the rules for its power supply
research.proposedSummary: Meta announced a larger Richland Parish campus. The original utility approval includes specific protections for other customers, while a separate expansion application remains a distinct proceeding. Explain the original order in plain language and distinguish announced savings from measured bills. Report the September 16 procedural outcome from the official minutes: the commission vacated the August 6 ruling, accepted the stipulation and deemed the motion for immediate review moot. Say that this did not decide the application. Attribute the December 16 date to the May scheduling order. Use the supported local business, school and water context with clear attribution.

claims.text: LED announced the original $10 billion AI data-center plan in Richland Parish on December 4, 2024.

supports.excerpt:
December 4, 2024 • [News Release](https://www.opportunitylouisiana.gov/news/category/news-release)

# Meta Selects Northeast Louisiana as Site of $10 Billion Artificial Intelligence Optimized Data Center; Governor Jeff Landry Calls Investment ‘A New Chapter’ for State

- ##### **Project is expected to result in 500 or more direct new jobs, more than 1,000 indirect jobs and 5,000 construction workers at peak.**

- ##### **Expansive technology campus will occupy 4 million square feet on the 2,250-acre former Franklin Farm mega site.**

- ##### **Entergy worked with Meta to address energy needs, and Meta will match its electricity use with 100% clean and renewable energy.**


RICHLAND PARISH, La. – Facebook and Instagram parent company Meta announced it will build a $10 billion artificial intelligence data center in northeast Louisiana,

claims.text: The original announcement places the former Franklin Farm site between Rayville and Delhi in Richland Parish, about 30 miles east of Monroe.

supports.excerpt: Meta projects the data center will support 500 or more direct new jobs in Richland Parish. LED estimates the project will result in the creation of more than 1,000 indirect jobs, for a total of more than 1,500 potential new jobs in the Northeast Region. The company estimates 5,000 construction workers at peak of construction on the 2,250-acre former Franklin Farm megasite that sits between the municipalities of Rayville and Delhi, about 30 miles east of Monroe.

claims.text: LED reported on July 13, 2026 that Meta announced a commitment exceeding $50 billion, nearly 10 million square feet and 5 gigawatts of IT capacity in Richland Parish.

supports.excerpt: HOLLY RIDGE, La. – Meta announced it is committing more than $50 billion to its Richland Parish Data Center project, expanding the campus to nearly 10 million square feet and 5 gigawatts of IT capacity.

claims.text: The July announcement projects 7,500 peak construction jobs and approximately 1,000 operational jobs. These are projections, not a verified employment count.

supports.excerpt: The project is expected to support 7,500 construction jobs at peak construction and approximately 1,000 operational jobs. Louisiana Economic Development estimates the project will result in an additional 1,900 indirect new jobs for over 2,900 new job opportunities in the Northeast Region.

claims.text: The original LED announcement expected Meta to use the Act 730 data-center equipment incentive and Quality Jobs program; this does not prove an executed project agreement or realized rebate.

supports.excerpt: The company is expected to take advantage of a new Louisiana incentive program, established by Act 730, that offers qualifying projects a state and local sales and use tax rebate on the purchase or lease of data center equipment. Meta is also expected to participate in the state’s Quality Jobs program.

claims.text: The LPSC official synopsis says Order U-37425 accepted a settlement approving generation and transmission resources subject to conditions.

supports.excerpt: Order No. U-37425 accepts the settlement entered into by Entergy Louisiana, LPSC Staff, Sierra Club, Walmart, and Southern Renewable Energy Association, approving the generation and transmission resources proposed in connection with service to a customer project in North Louisiana, subject to certain conditions.

claims.text: The May 14 order concerns requested generation and transmission certification for Evest LLC in Richland Parish adjacent to the Laidley facility; it is a procedural order.

supports.excerpt: On March 25, 2026, Entergy Louisiana LLC (“ELL” or the “Company”) filed its application seeking certification of generation and transmission resources needed to serve a substantial new load proposed for Evest LLC, a customer seeking to locate a large hyperscale data center in Richland Parish, adjacent to the facility currently being developed by Laidley, LLC (“Application”).

claims.text: The May 14, 2026 LPSC order directs a schedule for consideration of the application at the December 16, 2026 Business and Executive Session. Recheck the current agenda before attending.

supports.excerpt: 1. The Administrative Hearings Division shall establish a procedural schedule in LPSC Docket No. U-37882 that provides for Commission consideration of the Application at the December 16, 2026 Business and Executive Session.

claims.text: LED identifies SourceLouisiana.com as the registration route for businesses seeking project subcontracting opportunities, without guaranteeing a contract.

supports.excerpt: This commitment to Louisiana also extends to the state’s business community. The company has designated Source Louisiana as its primary portal for subcontracting opportunities on the project, helping connect local companies to its growing supplier network. Launched last year, the free platform gives in-state companies greater visibility into major project opportunities by showcasing their services, certifications and capacity. Interested businesses can register at [SourceLouisiana.com (opens external page in a new window)](http://sourcelouisiana.com/).

claims.text: The July LED release describes a recent utility agreement for seven gas generating plants and other resources, with projected customer savings. The announcement alone does not certify those resources.

supports.excerpt: As the project scope grows, Meta and power company Entergy Louisiana are continuing and expanding their commitment to investing in the communities where they operate. The companies’ [recent agreement (opens external page in a new window)](https://www.entergy.com/news/entergy-louisiana-announces-a-new-agreement-with-meta-that-will-deliver-an-additional-2b-in-customer-savings) will fund seven new natural gas-fueled generating plants, three grid-scale batteries, potential nuclear development, including a project to increase the output of Entergy Louisiana’s Waterford 3 nuclear facility and other purchased power, and is expected to deliver more than $2 billion in savings for Entergy Louisiana customers, far exceeding the $650 million [previously announced (opens external page in a new window)](https://www.entergy.com/news/entergy-louisiana-breaks-ground-on-new-state-of-the-art-generation-facilities-to-power-reliability-growth-and-innovation).

claims.text: The LPSC August 12, 2026 minutes record a 3:1 vote in U-37882 to reverse the tribunal ruling and vacate the subpoena, rendering the motion to quash moot. This was a subpoena decision, not approval of the generation and transmission application.

th

claims.text: The original utility order identifies Laidley LLC as Meta Platforms subsidiary and the customer for the Richland Parish project.

supports.excerpt:
On October 30, 2024, Entergy Louisiana, LLC (“ELL” or the “Company”) filed with the
Louisiana Public Service Commission (“LPSC” or “Commission”) its Application for Approval
of Generation and Transmission Resources Proposed in Connection with Service to a Significant
Customer Project in North Louisiana, Including Proposed Rider, and Request for Timely
Treatment (“Application”), in which the Company asked for, among other things, approval by the
Commission for the Company to construct the generation and transmission resources needed to
serve significant new load associated with a data center being developed by Meta Platforms, Inc.,
through its subsidiary, Laidley LLC (the “Customer”), in Richland Parish, Louisiana (the
“Project”).
supports.section: Order page 1, project and customer identity

claims.text: The original order makes generator cost recovery subject to later review of actual costs and requires Entergy to provide quarterly construction schedule and cost updates.

supports.excerpt:
The retail revenue requirement associated with the Planned Generators (to be determined
at the time each is proposed to be included in rates and subject to change in a prudence
review of their actual costs) is deemed eligible for recovery in the first billing cycle of the
month following commercial operation of each of the Planned Generators through the
applicable mechanisms of the Company’s then-effective Formula Rate Plan (“FRP”).
Entergy has a continuing obligation to prudently manage the construction of the Planned
Generators and will provide quarterly updates to Commission Staff on the status of the
construction of the Planned Generators, including the schedule, costs, and other critical
associated activities.
supports.section: Order page 6, rate recovery and construction monitoring

claims.text: Commission Staff explicitly did not recommend approval of the electric service agreement and related agreements; the Commission retains oversight of how Entergy manages them.

supports.excerpt:
Staff explicitly is not expressing approval of, or recommending that the Commission
approve, the ESA and the Related Agreements.  The Parties reserve all rights afforded by
applicable law and the Commission retains fully its authority consistent with applicable
law regarding prudence as it relates to the ESA and Related Agreements, including but not
limited to ELL’s management of the ESA and the Related Agreements and any ELL
decision to amend or to cancel any or all of those agreements or any provision of any or all
of those agreements.

claims.text: The original order requires Entergy to obtain and enforce parent guarantees and other security. If the customer terminates early, Entergy must seek to make use of excess capacity and seek approval for how to use the early termination fee after receiving it.

supports.excerpt:
ELL will ensure that all Parent Guaranty agreements are obtained and fully executed and
will timely and prudently enforce its rights with respect to the Parent Guaranty agreements
and other collateral security, including but not limited to the Credit Insurance.
In the event the Customer terminates its ESA, ELL will prudently seek to maximize the
value of any excess capacity that may result from the termination and, following receipt of
the Early Termination Fee in the event of early termination, make a filing with the
Commission for approval of the manner in which ELL proposes to utilize the Early
Termination Fee.
supports.section: Order page 7, parent guarantees and early termination

claims.text: The original order says material transmission upgrades required solely because of the project must not be included in other customers rates. This is a specific cost rule, not a promise that household bills cannot change.

supports.excerpt:
ELL will conduct appropriate analyses regarding the interplay between the Customer’s
Project and ELL’s transmission system and will install power quality monitoring
equipment on the substation serving the Customer’s Project.  To the extent material
upgrades are required to the transmission system solely as a result of the Customer's
Project, the costs of those upgrades will not be included in the rates of customers other
than the Customer.

claims.text: LED reported in July 2026 that Meta had contracted more than $1.6 billion with Louisiana businesses. This is a reported contract value, not verified money paid out.

supports.excerpt: Since construction began, Meta has prioritized working with Louisiana companies, already contracting more than $1.6 billion with local businesses and supporting workforce development across the region.

claims.text: LED reported that construction-related sales tax revenue enabled supplemental payments to Richland Parish teachers and staff. This release does not establish the amount paid to an individual teacher.

supports.excerpt: The project’s economic impact is also reaching local classrooms. Increased sales tax revenues generated during construction have enabled Richland Parish Schools to provide record supplemental payments to teachers and staff, strengthening the district’s ability to attract and retain educators while investing in student success. Meta is paying tens of millions of dollars in taxes every year supporting local schools, roads, law enforcement, and public services.

claims.text: LED reported a plan to return 100% of facility water consumption to local watersheds and invest in restoration and water infrastructure. This announcement does not establish actual withdrawals, a water allocation or project permits.

supports.excerpt: The company is further advancing sustainability efforts, with plans to return 100% of the facility’s water consumption to local watersheds and invest in wetland restoration and water infrastructure projects across the region.

claims.text: LED reported a $215 million commitment to bill assistance and residential energy efficiency over the utility agreement, and a commitment to fund up to 2.5 GW of renewable energy. These are attributed commitments, not verified completed spending.

supports.excerpt: Meta is expanding its support for Entergy’s affordability initiatives, contributing $215 million to its The Power to Care bill assistance program and residential energy efficiency programs over the course of the agreement and committing to fund up to 2.5 GW of clean, renewable energy.
